title: Reference
description: Every kind, table, relation, stage and check of a product, generated from its schema and checks.

title: Record's data file
description: Where each record is kept: its kind's data file in its product's data folder, as the engine that loaded the folder knows it and the desktop reveals or opens it.

title: Use case
description: A use case as its readers read it: all of it at once as a tree (its requirements, each with its tests and the steps that fulfill it, and its flows by interface, each with its steps path by path and its flow test) with the record asked about; a capability's list reads each use case's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Product
description: A product as its readers read it: its own details and roles, its business outcomes with the capabilities serving each, its domains, its product kinds with their fields, its product relations, its open questions with what they are about, and its interfaces with the flows through each and the use cases with none, by capability; and every product as a space.

title: Pattern
description: A pattern as its readers read it: all of it at once (its settings in order, its rules by ID, each with its tests per following domain) with the record asked about; a product's list reads each pattern's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Who follows it is Pattern following's. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Standard
description: A standard as its readers read it: all of it at once (its rules by ID, each with the records that meet it and its tests) with the record asked about; a product's list reads each standard's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Domain
description: A domain as its readers read it: all of it at once (its capabilities in order, each with the outcomes it serves and its use cases; its terms bottom-up, each with the terms it builds on; its domain services, each with its service and tests; its repositories, each with the aggregate it persists) with the record asked about; a product's list reads each domain's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Specification
description: A specification as its readers read it: all of it at once (the aggregates it reads, its predicate with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses, its test with the test data sets it starts from) with the record asked about; a domain's list reads each specification's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Aggregate
description: An aggregate as its readers read it: all of it at once (its entities, the root first, each with its fields, the entities it holds, its data model, the commands that change it and its tables; its invariants, each with its test; the domain events that happen to it, each with the commands that raise it and the policies that hear it) with the record asked about; a domain's list reads each aggregate's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Domain event
description: A domain event as its readers read it: all of it at once (the fields it carries in order, its event type with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses, the commands that raise it and the policies that hear it) with the record asked about; an aggregate's list reads each event's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Command
description: A command as its readers read it: all of it at once (the events it raises, the specifications it checks and the domain services it calls; its handler; its policies, each with the event it hears, its event handler and its test; the endpoints that expose it; the other aggregates it also changes, each with its reason) with the record asked about; an entity's list reads each command's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Value object
description: A value object as its readers read it: all of it at once (its fields in order, its constraints by ID each with its test and the test data sets it starts from, its value type with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses) with the record asked about; a product's list reads each value object's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Read model
description: A read model as its readers read it: all of it at once (its fields in order, what it reads, calls and is fed by, its queries by ID each with what it selects by and calls and its handler, its projection and its reader, each piece of code with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses) with the record asked about; a domain's list reads each read model's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: View
description: A view as its readers read it: all of it at once (its requirements by ID, each with its tests and the test data sets they start from) with the record asked about; a product's list reads each view's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Endpoint
description: An endpoint as its readers read it: all of it at once (its handler with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses, and its API requirements by ID, each with its tests and the test data sets they start from) with the record asked about; a command's or query's list reads each endpoint that exposes it, by ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Integration
description: An integration as its readers read it: all of it at once (its adapter with the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses, and its integration tests by ID with the test data sets they start from) with the record asked about; a product's list reads each of its integrations, by ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: UI component
description: A UI component as its readers read it: all of it at once (its own details, the views it renders, the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses) with the record asked about; a product's list reads each UI component's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Business outcome
description: One business outcome as its readers read it: its statement, measure and target, the tests and records that measure it, and the capabilities that serve it.

title: Test data set
description: A test data set as its readers read it: all of it at once with the tests that start from it; a domain's list reads each set's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Table
description: A table as its readers read it: all of it at once (the entity, read model or domain it sits under, its keys in order, the standard rules it meets and the packages it uses); the list under an entity, a read model or a domain reads each table's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Extension record
description: One record of a product's own kind as its readers read it: its kind and the kind's label, the record it sits under, its title and declared fields, the links it starts by relation and the packages it uses.

title: Entry point
description: One entry point whole: its own details, the packages it uses and the standard rules it meets.

title: Tooling
description: One tooling record whole: its own details, the packages it uses and the standard rules it meets.

title: Storage requirement
description: A storage requirement as its readers read it: all of it at once (the aggregate or read model it is about, the repository or reader that builds it with the data store that names, its storage requirement tests with the test data sets each starts from) with the record asked about; an aggregate's or read model's list reads each requirement's ID and title; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Data store
description: A data store as its readers read it: all of it at once (the product or domain it sits under, the integration that reaches it, and the repositories, readers and tables stored in it); a product's or domain's list reads each store's ID, title and kind; the editor's next ID reads the IDs in use. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Problems
description: A product's problems as its Checks panel reads them: its own problems by check, errors first, the problems that belong to no product by check, and its errors and warnings counted. Its own shape, built from the checks' run (never stored; worked out on every load) and the records' places in their products.

title: Check view
description: A check as its readers read it: the Check view reads one whole by its name (Lathe's or a product's own); a product's list reads the checks that run on it, Lathe's first and then its own, each in run order with its severity and summary. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Limits
description: A product's limits, its own or the defaults: the most children of one kind a record should hold and the most entities an aggregate should hold.

title: Essential review
description: A product's essential records alone, grouped by domain in ID order with those in no domain last, each with its kind, title and lead text, for a reviewer who asks of each whether someone who knows the domain but not software would recognize and care about it. Worked out from the data on every read; never kept.

title: Record summaries
description: Every record of a product's space (its own and those of no product) as its pages name it: its kind, title, parent, product and domain, its group heading, a test's state and level, what it names in code, its data file and line and a digest of its data; and the links among them both ways. No field beyond these: a page reads its record's fields through its aggregate's own query.

title: Folder tree
description: Each product's nav tree: Shared, then each domain's stages, in each stage one folder per kind (SP03) with the records that start a branch there and what folds under each, placed by DS03; then the kinds outside the stages. The nav, Quick open and the graph's tree read it.

title: Graph map
description: One map per product and layout: the folder tree (DS04) laid out once per load by DS05 (Tree), DS07 (Nested) or DS12 (Map, the product's districts with each record holding its composition), every node with its place, size and label.

title: ERD
description: A product's one ERD: its domains as regions, each aggregate a boundary around its entities (the root first) with their fields and types, and the has-one, has-many and reference-by-ID lines between entities. The app lays it out once per answer and draws it.

title: Record history
description: The commits that changed a record's data, read from git on each request.

title: Spaces
description: Every product as a space in the rail, with its look and place.

title: Record changes
description: What changed in a product's records between a baseline (the last commit, where the branch left the default branch, or a commit the app noted) and the data now, by record: each added, removed or changed, with its own changed fields, its parts and the links it starts. Computed on each ask.

title: Workspace
description: Every product's records, links, problems and coverage, as one load of the data files gives them: `Workspace` in `lathe/src/types.ts`. Filled from the data files whenever they change.

title: Keymap
description: Every keyboard command with the keys that run it on this platform as the person bound them: the defaults in code (the keymap's commands) with the Key bindings in their place, which every key, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, every hint and the desktop menu read.

title: Themes
description: Every theme, which one is in use and the color mode.

title: Recent folders
description: The recent folders, latest first, as File › Open Recent and the Dock menu list them.

title: Claude Code sessions
description: A folder's saved Claude Code sessions, from Claude Code's own saved sessions, each with its title, when it was last written, and whether another Claude client may have it open.

title: Reader's view
description: What a window shows the Reader: which view it is on, the focused record, the stage, the record selected on the stage or in the wiki card, and whether the wiki card is open.

title: Window's chat
description: A product window's chat as the view draws it: its session, its status, its permission mode, the Lathe tools it has (how many and from which Lathe, or why they did not load) and its items, sent whole when the view loads and then as patches.

title: Meta model
description: Lathe's kinds with each product's own, in reading order, the six stages, every pair of kinds each relation may link with its words both ways, and each kind's fields: what every view names a kind, places it in its stage, words a link and draws a field by. What the schema declares, never the records.

title: Voice support
description: Whether a window can dictate: on-device recognition on this Mac (macOS 26 or later, the speech helper built and able), why not when it cannot, the microphone's permission, and whether end-of-turn detection can read the voice.

title: Chat skills
description: The skills and slash commands Claude Code would find for the window's folder: the folder's, the Owner's, the installed plugins' and Lathe's, and its own that work without a dialog, each with a one-line description.

title: Coverage
description: A product's coverage, scope by scope (its records outside every domain, then each domain): per obligation kind how many are designed, built, proved and not automated yet out of the total, its tests by state, and its gaps. Built from the checks' run.

title: Coverage gaps
description: Each obligation not designed, built or proved, with what it lacks.

title: Tests by state
description: Each domain's tests by state: automated, manual and not automated yet.

title: Owed pattern rules
description: Each pattern rule each following domain owes.

title: File facts
description: Each test and technical record that names a file: whether the file exists, and whether a test's file names its ID. With them, each operation's and view's address and whether the files of what implements it name it, and each address the code serves.

title: Record trace
description: One record's traceability, as the Record view pattern's Traceability section shows it: an obligation's chain (what designs it, the technical records that build it, each built or not, and the tests that prove it) and how each owing domain stands on it; a use case's UC requirements judged; a test's run by; and its other links both ways by relation.

title: Stored record facts
description: Each part a kind of record kept in its own storage should have in the file it names (the kind itself, each field, each primary, unique and foreign key), and whether that file defines it.

title: Pattern following
description: A pattern's followings as their readers read them: a following whole (the value, or the reason it does not apply, its follower gives each setting of its pattern); the patterns a domain or use case follows; and a pattern's followers by domain, as the pattern's Followed by reads them: whether the domain itself follows it, and each of its use cases that does, each with its setting values. Its own shape, not the aggregate's.

title: Serves
description: The business outcomes each record serves, as a record's Serves line and the Trace's branches read them: worked out from the records on every read through the use cases that reach each record (the Serves reach), never stored; and a product's records that serve an outcome, with those of its aggregates, read models and obligations none reaches.

title: Trace
description: A product's use cases as the Trace stage reads them, one line each from the business outcomes its capability serves to its acceptance tests: its UC requirements with their gaps and tests, the aggregates its steps change and the read models they read (the Serves reach), its flows with each step's design (what it fulfills, its view and view requirements, its operations and API requirements, its integrations) and technical chain (interface parts, operations or the product's own channels, the records that handle them, what reads and writes the data, where it is stored, and the connectors to integrations), its flow tests, the lower obligations its tests rest on, and its status per stage. Its own shape, built from the records and the checks' run (gaps and tests, worked out on every load).
